In the Mahabharata, she is described as the wife of Bhishma Pitamaha and the mother of Vichitravirya. When Bhishma was lying on the bed of arrows, he had a vision of Aparajita, who granted him a boon that he could choose the time of his death. Later, he chose to die when Arjuna shot an arrow at him during the Kurukshetra war.

In the Puranas, Aparajita is described as a goddess who personifies victory over all obstacles and adversities. She is often depicted with ten arms, each holding a weapon, and is sometimes identified with the goddess Durga. The story goes that once, she was cursed by a demon to be born as a woman. Despite this, she continued to fight against evil and ultimately defeated the demon, earning the name Aparajita, which means 'invincible'.
